approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill sets up a national framework to protect the interests of people not yet born from being overshadowed by short-term political cycles.
It would oblige government agencies to weigh the long-term effects of their choices and create an independent watchdog to speak for future Australians, along with a public consultation process.
The bill's explanatory memorandum does not specify how the public consultation would be run or when the framework would take effect.
Introduces a federal framework for future generations' wellbeing.
Imposes a duty on public bodies to consider long-term impacts and collaborate more effectively.
Establishes an independent Commissioner for Future Generations.
Requires a public consultation led by the Commissioner to shape Australia's long-term vision.
Public bodies, the Commissioner, and the Australian public would be affected.

The prime minister agreed on intergenerational equity and announced a $177 billion reduction in forecast debt, a 20% cut to student debt benefiting three million Australians by an average of $5,000, and investments in education, housing, jobs, and climate action. He committed to reviewing the Wellbeing of Future Generations Bill.
